clue.text: Horns, etc, and other dashboard features?

blocks.note: first meaning: the musical instruments chosen for a piece, horns among them
second meaning: the dials and gauges in front of a driver

explanation.surface: A list of the things on a car's dashboard, starting with the hooter.
explanation.walkthrough: Horns look like car horns beside the dashboard, but they belong to the orchestra; the word covers both the band's scoring and a car's gauges.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the scoring of music for particular players and the set of measuring dials fitted to a vehicle or machine.

clue.text: It's used for bringing liquid to some degree

definitions.text: It's used for bringing liquid to some degree

blocks.note: surface reading: raising a drink or solution only partly, to some extent
setter's reading: a degree of temperature, so this warms water up

explanation.surface: A vague description of something that only half does a job with a liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some degree' sounds like 'partly', but here a degree is a step on the thermometer.
explanation.definitionFit: This electric element sits in a hot-water tank and warms the water inside it to a set temperature.

clue.text: Emotion - it sent men wild

indicators.note: something gone wild is out of control, so the letters break out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something stirred up such feeling that the men went berserk.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling or tender emotion is a plain synonym for this noun.

clue.text: Kick you get from a Martini?

definitions.text: Kick you get from a Martini?

blocks.clueFragment: Kick you get from a Martini
blocks.note: surface reading: the alcoholic punch of a vermouth cocktail
setter's reading: the Martini-Henry, a Victorian army rifle, which kicks back when fired

explanation.surface: Someone notes the punch a strong cocktail packs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Martini-Henry was the British army's rifle in the late 1800s; the drink is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's backward jolt on firing is called its kick, the same thing as this noun.

clue.text: Fail to spot schoolteacher

blocks.note: first meaning: overlook
second meaning: what British pupils call a female teacher

explanation.surface: A pupil gets away with something the teacher never notices.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means overlook, and children in British schools address a woman teacher by this title.

clue.text: Batsman unlikely to be out?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cricketer hard to dismiss
setter's reading: out on strike, which a worker who refuses to strike is not

explanation.surface: A cricketer with a sound defence who rarely loses his wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman at the bowler's end is not facing, so he can seldom be dismissed; and 'out' is also how workers on strike are described.
explanation.definitionFit: The batsman standing at the bowler's end, not receiving the ball, carries this name in cricket.

clue.text: Scholar of little consequence?

blocks.note: first meaning: a university teacher or researcher
second meaning: of theoretical interest only, as in a question that is purely this

explanation.surface: A dig at a learned person who doesn't matter much.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a university researcher; as an adjective it describes a point that no longer has practical relevance.

clue.text: Girl from Perthshire, near Dunkeld

indicators.note: 'from' says the letters come out of the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the run straddles the end of the county name and the next word
surface padding: a small Perthshire town that completes the picture and supplies no letters

explanation.surface: A lass whose home is in the Perthshire countryside close to Dunkeld.
explanation.walkthrough: Dunkeld is a small Perthshire town and contributes no letters; it just finishes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's given name, and crosswords often use 'girl' for any female first name.

clue.text: Repairs end at heel, darned using these?

definitions.text: Repairs end at heel, darned using these?

indicators.note: a repair puts things back together in a new way, so the letters are refashioned

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sock worn through at the heel gets mended with the usual sewing kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the tools for darning a sock's heel are asked for, while the same words supply every letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Darning a hole is done by stitching wool or cotton through it with a sewing pin that has an eye.

clue.text: Excitable chap in charge

blocks.note: a chap is a man
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: The fellow running things is a nervy, overexcited type.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wildly energetic and agitated is described by this adjective, a near synonym of excitable.

clue.text: Language spoken by aliens she translated

indicators.note: translating turns words into a different form, so the letters are rendered in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman interprets the speech of visitors from another planet.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the main tongue of Sri Lanka, spoken by its largest ethnic group.

clue.text: Mostly growing fruit

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: raising, as in raising crops, means growing

explanation.surface: A description of fruit that is largely still ripening.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a familiar dried fruit, so the answer is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Oriental leather, fantastic, out of this world

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or wild, so the letters take a fanciful new order

blocks.note: E stands for east, the Orient
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for some wonderful hide goods from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heavenly, delicate and unearthly is a fair match for the idiom about seeming not of this planet.

clue.text: Prince changed to shy chap, becoming an antisocial type

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for prince
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal turns into a timid fellow and then something darker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a personality disorder marked by lack of empathy and hostile conduct toward others fits the description.

clue.text: Thought to be not entirely wideawake

indicators.note: not entirely says only a part of the following word is used

blocks.note: letters two to five of the word

explanation.surface: Someone is judged to be a little less than fully alert.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or concept in the mind is a straightforward synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Houseplant in part is said to be hybrid

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross-bred mix, so the letters are mixed into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Talk of an indoor plant that is reportedly partly a cross-breed.
explanation.definitionFit: This tough broad-leaved plant was a fixture of Victorian and later British parlours, a classic indoor pot plant.

clue.text: Sports car, inappropriate conveyance for stylish marriage?

blocks.note: first meaning: a small car with room for driver and one passenger
second meaning: the bicycle made for two in the old song, offered because the singer cannot afford a carriage

explanation.surface: A sporty little car would be the wrong vehicle for a grand wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The song Daisy Bell runs: 'It won't be a stylish marriage, I can't afford a carriage, But you'll look sweet upon the seat of a bicycle made for two.'
explanation.definitionFit: Both a roadster and a tandem bicycle carry exactly a pair of riders, the literal sense of the word.

clue.text: Ventured to get seasoned journalist to go round South Africa

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: seasoned, of wood or people, means hardened
ZA is the international code for South Africa
ED, editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: An experienced reporter took a chance on touring South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture a guess or opinion is to risk it, the past tense matching this verb.

clue.text: Ruined hut surrounded by a stench, possibly from birds

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the following word's letters are jumbled
being surrounded means sitting inside what follows
possibly hints at one of several possible arrangements of the letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A derelict shed reeks, perhaps because of the birds nesting there.
explanation.definitionFit: These small tree-climbing songbirds are a kind of bird, so the plural answer is an example of birds.

clue.text: Car seen in France or Germany

blocks.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
taken as written
D, for Deutschland, is Germany's vehicle code

explanation.surface: A make of car spotted on roads across the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford is a major car manufacturer, so a vehicle of that make is a car by example.

clue.text: Relative almost appearing on commercial in the altogether?

indicators.note: almost means nearly whole, so the final letter of the relative is cut

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A family member nearly shows up in a TV advert wearing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In the altogether' is a British idiom for stark naked, and the answer means without clothes.

clue.text: Sacrificial ox pirate offered - he’s attempting to make amends

indicators.note: something sacrificed is given up and destroyed, so the words lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A buccaneer offers up a beast at the altar to atone for his crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate is to atone for a wrong, and the agent noun names the person doing that atoning.

clue.text: Quantity of sump oil used by French soldier

indicators.note: a quantity is a portion, so only some letters of the following words are taken

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of the first word and ends at the start of the last

explanation.surface: A soldier in France's army draws on the oil from an engine's sump.
explanation.walkthrough: The sump is the oil reservoir under a car engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Poilu, literally hairy one, was the nickname for a French infantryman, especially in the First World War.

clue.text: Men she’s about to ensnare

indicators.note: about means around or turned about, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is about to trap some men.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch something as if in a net is to entangle or trap it, a synonym of ensnare.

clue.text: Young man from office abandoning City

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it out, so those letters go

blocks.note: a bureau is an office or agency
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A lad quits his office job and leaves town.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the ancient city from the office word, taking out its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend or admirer, especially a fashionable young man, is this old-fashioned noun.

clue.text: Inferior trader hit badly

indicators.note: badly means poorly done, so the letters end up in a wrecked order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor-quality merchant has taken a heavy blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Of low quality, well below first class, is the meaning of this adjective, a synonym of inferior.

clue.text: Left a couple of articles in machine tool

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a pair of articles: the indefinite one and the definite one

explanation.surface: Some items were left behind inside a piece of workshop equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' sounds like objects, but here it means the grammar words a and the.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe spins a workpiece against a cutting blade, a standard workshop machine for shaping wood or metal.

clue.text: Having a stoop like a golfer?

definitions.text: Having a stoop like a golfer?

blocks.note: surface reading: bent forward in posture, as a golfer is over a putt
setter's reading: a golfer plays a round and carries a bag of clubs on the shoulder

explanation.surface: Golfers are said to hunch over their shots.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer: a golfer goes out for a round and has his clubs shouldered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a forward-curving upper back and drooping posture is described by this compound adjective.
